channel.title: AI News Radar
channel.description: A curated 24-hour radar of AI news: official releases, new models and high-signal discussion.

item.title: Anthropic spends $3.4B to snap up power generation equipment and boost energy supply for its data centers
item.description: Anthropic’s September deal with OnePWR Solutions, worth $3.4 billion, covers 1.7 GW of heavy-duty generator sets plus installation, described as the largest single power-equipment purchase by an AI company to date. (AIbase)

item.title: DeepSeek's open-source agent app Harness tops 1.54M daily active users: less than three months after launch, daily model consumption soars to 92T tokens
item.description: DeepSeek's open-source Harness agent framework reached 1.54 million daily active API users in under three months, consuming about 92 trillion tokens per day—roughly 60 million per user—and spawning some 35,000 custom plugins. (AIbase)

item.title: He Xi 2077 AI Deep Signal Weekly 2026 W45: Execution Foundation, Acceptance Debt, and the Boundaries of Memory
item.description: Covering November 2–8, 2026, the weekly digest distills 194 AI news items into agent execution foundations, acceptance debt, and memory boundaries, citing HEELO’s 46 tasks and Terminal-Bench’s roughly 30% benchmark problems as lingering verification work. (Daily Digest)

item.title: Google Messages kicks off major homepage overhaul: Gemini shortcut added, pinned chats and bottom search reworked
item.description: Google Messages is testing an Android homepage redesign that lifts pinned chat avatars to the top, turns search into a centered floating button that scales as you scroll, and moves the Gemini entry beside the top-right avatar. (AIbase)

item.title: MiniMax founder Yan Junjie: scaling post-training through extreme efficiency gains, and staying committed to open source until AGI is achieved
item.description: MiniMax founder Yan Junjie told Scottish Mortgage's Lawrence Burns China's top models reach about 95% of US frontier performance at one-tenth the cost, using inference savings from a roughly 500-person team to scale post-training and stay open source until AGI. (AIbase)

item.title: OpenAI raises $11 billion in new funding round at a $1.25 trillion valuation
item.description: OpenAI has raised $11 billion in a new round at a $1.25 trillion valuation, though TechCrunch reports this is only part of an unfinished plan that could reach roughly $20 billion. (AIbase)

item.title: SpaceXAI expands Grok Bot access to all SuperGrok and Cursor plans
item.description: SpaceXAI has widened Grok Bot access from SuperGrok Heavy, Cursor Ultra and Cursor Teams Premium to all three SuperGrok tiers plus Cursor Pro and Ultra, where the $20/month Pro bot runs in Cursor cloud computers and keeps working after shutdown. (AIbase)

item.title: xAI gives Grok Bot a full upgrade, focusing on Token efficiency and intelligence
item.description: xAI's Matt Palmer and Elon Musk announced on X that Grok Bot is getting a new round of underlying architecture and feature optimization focused on token efficiency and smarter behavior, cutting developer costs and improving logic accuracy on complex tasks while soliciting developer feedback. (AIbase)

item.title: How I fight AI mental exhaustion
item.description: By putting Claude Code and Codex tasks into a git-based markdown ticket queue and an owner inbox for human-judgment items, the author handles one ticket at a time and closes context after finishing, countering switching across 20 threads. (sergeykuhne.com)

item.title: anthropics/claude-quickstarts — A collection of projects designed to help developers quickly get started with building deployable applications using the Claude API
item.description: anthropics/claude-quickstarts bundles Claude API starter projects for a customer support agent, financial data analysis, Computer Use and Browser Use, plus a macOS-native computer-use reference implementation demonstrating tool definitions and prompt caching. (GitHub Trending)

item.title: Workbuddy refunds half of DeepSeek users' credits after quietly ending a discount, sparking backlash
item.description: Tencent Workbuddy apologized for ending its DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash discount without timely notice and will recalculate points spent from November 5 at 14:00 to November 8 at 23:59 at 50%, automatically refunding the difference within seven working days. (AIbase)

item.title: Llama-modchip: features a 284B DeepSeek chip, 64GB of memory, and no GPU
item.description: llama-modchip runs a 284B DeepSeek-V4-Flash model entirely on a 64GB CPU with zero GPUs, using under 59GiB of RAM and decoding at 9.1–14.7 tok/s across a 256K context window. (github.com)

item.title: OpenAI raises $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation
item.description: OpenAI raised roughly $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation—only 37% of its original $30 billion target—and the shortfall’s effects on Microsoft and NVIDIA are analyzed. (247wallst.com)

item.title: I'm Not Convinced the AI Bubble Exists
item.description: Rejecting the AI bubble as speculative, the author cites $1.9 trillion spent and at least $3 trillion committed by AI companies, plus Anthropic’s S-1 showing $2.08 revenue per $1 of compute.

item.title: Why I don't use large language models for programming
item.description: Why I don't use large language models for programming (www.polso.info)

item.title: Chinese AI's Big Moment: Qwen4 Beats Opus 5.5 on Benchmarks for the First Time, With Cost-Effectiveness as Its Biggest Weapon
item.description: Alibaba's Qwen4-Flash scored 49.9 on the GameFeel Bench game-development creativity evaluation, edging past Opus5.5xHigh's 47.2 while costing about $0.4 versus $2.6 per equivalent task, with Qwen4-27B at $0.16. (AIbase)

item.title: Silicon Valley Promises AI Will Cure Disease. Drugmaker CEOs Aren't Buying It
item.description: WSJ reports that Silicon Valley's claims that AI will cure disease are meeting skepticism from drugmaker CEOs, laying out both sides' arguments and evidence over AI's prospects in drug discovery.

item.title: Two years after the new Siri slipped, Apple's AI chief is weighing an exit
item.description: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reports Mike Rockwell, who leads new Siri after Vision Pro, is considering exiting as Siri engineering VP or leaving Apple next year, with Amar Subramanya and Sebastien Marineau as possible successors after Siri's two-year delay. (AIbase)

item.title: Goldman Sachs is pulling Claude Code from its bankers and traders
item.description: Goldman Sachs is pulling Claude Code and GitHub access from bankers and traders, returning it to about 12,000 engineers weeks before taking Anthropic public; traders had used the AI agents to monitor client trading flows and model markets.

item.title: Pinning Down AI at the Ballot Box: How the US Midterms Could Trigger a Tech Stock Crash
item.description: Thursday night's U.S. stock slide marked a turning point for the two-year AI rally, as midterm-election politics weigh on tech valuations and threaten a broader selloff across AI-linked shares. (AIbase)
